caption:
Happy 40th Birthday to my best friend, my partner, and the love of my life @harjotghuman . ❤️

Over 20 years ago, we met as friends, and somehow that friendship turned into the greatest love story I could have ever imagined.

People always say you fall in love with a person, but I believe you also fall in love with their community. I fell in love with the way you loved your family, your friends, and everyone around you. Your kindness, your positivity, and your heart have always been what make you so special.

Thank you for believing in me long before anyone else did. Thank you for standing beside me through every crazy dream, every risk, every setback, and every success. Everything we’ve built has never been because of me—it’s because of us.

Today, this is what 40 looks like: a beautiful family, lifelong friendships, our incredible daughter Miri, and a life filled with love. I wouldn’t trade it for anything.

Life will always throw challenges our way, but one thing I know for certain is that we’ll keep facing them together—stronger, wiser, and hopefully a little younger at heart every year.

Watching you become the most incredible mother has been one of the greatest joys of my life. Miri is already becoming a little version of you, and I couldn’t ask for a better role model for her.

You are kind. You are beautiful. You are resilient. You light up every room you walk into.

(And yes… when you get mad, everyone knows it. 😂❤️)

Happy Birthday, my love. Here’s to 40, and to 50, 60, 70, 80, and beyond. I can’t wait to keep growing old—and young at heart—with you.

I love you forever. ❤️

caption:
The other day, I was in the men’s washroom doing my business when a couple of guys walked in.

There was some kind of team-building competition going on, and one guy asked the other, “How’s your team doing?”

He goes, “Ah, I don’t know… I think we’re gonna lose. We got a couple of girls on our team.”

They chuckled.

Then he goes, “They don’t even know how to throw.”

More laughs.

And I’m sitting there thinking…

Yo, shut the hell up.

I don’t know why, but that really got to me.

Maybe it’s because I have a daughter now.

And the thought of someone one day making her feel like she’s less capable, less strong, or that her team is somehow worse just because she’s a girl… that doesn’t sit right with me.

It’s crazy how becoming a dad changes you.

Things you might have ignored before suddenly hit different.

Because now I look at the world through her eyes too.

And I hope she grows up knowing that she belongs wherever she wants to be.

And that no one gets to decide what she’s capable of before she even gets a chance to show them.

caption:
44 looks a little different this year.

Two weeks ago, we found out my dad has cancer.

We never expected it. Just days before, he was playing golf, hiking, taking road trips, and enjoying life. Then suddenly, our family found ourselves sitting in a hospital waiting for answers.

Life can change in an instant.

As a business owner, this past year has been one of the most difficult of my life. The restaurant industry has tested me in ways I never imagined. But when we found out about my dad, every business problem, every stress, every worry suddenly felt so small.

Because at the end of the day, all you truly have is family.

What makes this even harder is that six years ago, my mom battled cancer too. As a family, we know this journey. We know the fear, the uncertainty, the waiting, and the emotional roller coaster that comes with it.

But we also know strength.

We know resilience.

And we know hope.

My mom fought through it, and she continues to inspire us every day. That experience taught us that even in the darkest moments, there is always a reason to keep believing.

No amount of money, success, awards, followers, or opinions can replace the people you love.

My birthday wish this year is simple:

• Count your blessings.
• Spend time with family.
• Pray to whoever you believe in.
• Be kind.
• Be present.
• Never take a single day for granted.

Dad, thank you for everything you’ve done for our family. You’ve spent your life taking care of us. Now it’s our turn to take care of you.

Mom, thank you for showing us what courage looks like.

Today isn’t about getting older. It’s about gratitude, family, faith, and appreciating every moment we get with the people we love.

Please keep my dad in your prayers.

No matter what comes our way, we’ll face it together—with faith, gratitude, and Chardi Kala. ❤️🙏

caption:
Straight Talk with Rick.

You know… becoming a dad has changed my life in the best possible way.

Ever since my daughter was born, all I wanna do is be around her. Watch her grow. Teach her things. Be present for every little moment.

But at the same time, I’m balancing multiple businesses — restaurants, catering, media, content — and the reality is, there’s just never enough time in the day.

And honestly? This has probably been the hardest year I’ve ever seen in hospitality.

Not just for me — for everybody.

Over 4,600 restaurants have closed this year. Food costs are up. Rent is up. Gas is up. Labour is up. Everything keeps going up… but margins keep shrinking bite by bite.

People think restaurants are easy. They’re not.

They’re one of the hardest businesses in the world.

If I’m being real, I don’t even know if I’d do it again knowing what I know now… but we’re in it. This is year 10 for us, and we’re gonna keep pushing.

Because we’re doing this for the culture.
For the food.
For the people.
And because we’re telling our story on a plate.

So to every restaurant owner out there barely holding it together right now — I see you.

January, February, March, and April were brutal. But summer’s coming, and hopefully that’s our chance to rebuild, catch up, pay down debt, and breathe a little again.

So support local.

Go eat at your local spots.
Buy gift cards.
Share their content.
Tell people about the places you love.

Because small businesses are still struggling more than people realize.

And as for me…

Being a dad, a restaurateur, a creator, a businessman — all at once — it’s a lot.

Some days I’m exhausted.
Some days I’m not 100%.

But I still gotta show up.
Still gotta smile.
Still gotta lead.
Because people are depending on me.

Big shoutout to my wife for always holding me down and keeping me grounded.

And of course… to my daughter.

You changed my life.

caption:
Traditionally, Lohri was celebrated to mark the birth of a son.
But this year, we celebrated our daughter’s first Lohri and it was one of the most special moments of my life.

If you believe Lohri is only for boys, that belief needs reflection mentally, emotionally, and culturally. Celebration should never be limited by gender.

My daughter is 100% equal, 100% deserving, and 100% worthy of every tradition, blessing, and celebration just like any boy.

We celebrated Lohri the way it is meant to be celebrated
around the fire
with music and culture
with family and friends
with saag, goat curry, and food that brings people together
with gratitude, pride, and love

For those who may not know, Lohri is a Punjabi harvest festival celebrated in January. It marks the end of winter, the return of longer days, and a time to celebrate family, prosperity, and new beginnings through fire, food, music, and community.

Traditions should grow with our values, not against them.
Life is short. Celebrate fully. Celebrate fairly.

From a proud girl dad,
Happy Lohri to all daughters and all sons 🧡🔥

caption:
2016 isn’t just a trend to us, it was our landmark year.

I got the keys to an empty restaurant at 6660 Kennedy Rd in Mississauga with no experience in the food industry. Just faith, drive, and my family by my side.

We renovated it ourselves.
Learned the equipment ourselves.
Built the menu and brand from scratch.

What started as a pop up from our home kitchen, selling samosas out of my Jeep through WhatsApp, finally had a home.

Those early days were long.
Blood, sweat, tears, and insane hours.

Mom and I would prep, cook every single order, and then wash every single dish ourselves after closing. Every day.

And it wasn’t just us.
My whole family was working.

My sister would come in after her teaching job and fold samosas.
My dad would put up shelves, fix problems, and then head to or come from his shift on the line at the Chrysler plant.
My wife would come in before and after her radio show to prep and run front of house.
My cousins and aunts would jump in whenever we needed help, taking orders, washing dishes, chopping cilantro, folding samosas, doing whatever needed to be done.

Just a few months in we had two break ins back to back.
Smashed windows. Setbacks. Fear.

But that only gave us more resolve to build something real for our community.

Rick’s Good Eats quickly became more than a restaurant.
It became a place for culture and connection.

Sold out art shows.
Open mic nights.
Running food drives for local food banks.
Packed dinner rushes.
A true community hub.

From street-side samosa sales to catering tech companies, weddings, and events, 2016 was the foundation of what you see today.

This was the year the dream found a home.

WE MADE TORONTO LIFE’S TOP 10

We’re incredibly honoured to share that Rick’s Good Eats landed TOP 10 on Toronto Life’s

This moment means a lot — because this samosa is personal.

On Sundays, the air would be filled with the smell of jerk chicken smoking in someone’s backyard, music playing, families outside. And being able to pull up anywhere in B-Town and grab a jerk chicken rice was always a delight.

That flavour stuck with me.

So when it came time to build our menu, the jerk chicken samosa had to exist.
It’s my tribute to B-Town — to the neighbours, the culture, and the way food connected us long before we ever called it fusion.

To see it recognized by @torontolife is surreal.

caption:
🌶️🧀 CHILLI CHEESE TOAST
Crispy bottom. Gooey top. Pure comfort.

⸻

Ingredients

• 2 thick slices sourdough bread
• 1 tbsp tomatoes, finely chopped
• Onions, finely chopped (to taste)
• 2 green chillies, finely chopped
• 4 tbsp cilantro, chopped (plus more for garnish)
• ¼ cup mozzarella & cheddar, grated
• ½ cup salted butter, room temperature
• 1 tsp garlic powder
• 1 tsp red chilli flakes
• 1 tsp black pepper
• 1 tsp chaat masala (plus more for garnish)

⸻

Method

1️⃣ In a bowl, mix softened butter with green chillies, cilantro, garlic powder, chilli flakes, black pepper, and chaat masala.
2️⃣ Spread about 2 tbsp of the spiced butter onto each slice of sourdough.
3️⃣ Top with grated cheese, tomatoes, and onions.
4️⃣ Heat a large pan with a lid over medium-low heat and lightly oil the base.
5️⃣ Place bread cheese-side up in the pan and let the bottom crisp slowly.
6️⃣ Add a few tablespoons of water to the pan, cover with a lid, and let the toast steam until the cheese is melty, bubbly, and irresistible.
7️⃣ Finish with a pinch of chaat masala and fresh cilantro.

⸻

✨ Crispy. Cheesy. Spicy.
Serve hot and enjoy!

caption:
Cranberry Chutney (Holiday Upgrade) 🍒🔥

This is my Indian-style cranberry chutney — sweet, tangy, lightly spicy, and finished with a hot mustard-chili ghee tarka. Once you make this, plain cranberry sauce is done.

⸻

Ingredients

Chutney
	•	2 cups fresh cranberries
	•	¼ cup water
	•	¾ cup sugar
	•	Juice of 1 orange
	•	Zest of 1 orange
	•	Pinch of salt
	•	1 tsp garam masala
	•	1 tsp roasted fenugreek seeds, ground
	•	1 tbsp apple cider vinegar

Tarka
	•	1–2 tbsp ghee
	•	1 tsp mustard seeds
	•	1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder

⸻

Method

Add cranberries, water, sugar, orange juice, orange zest, and salt to a saucepan.
Simmer 7–8 minutes until the cranberries burst.

Lightly smash for texture.

Add garam masala, ground fenugreek, and apple cider vinegar.
Cook 2–3 minutes until glossy and jammy. Remove from heat.

In a separate pan, heat ghee on high.
Add mustard seeds and Kashmiri chili, bloom for 15–20 seconds.

Pour the hot tarka over the chutney and fold in. Done.

⸻

Tips
	•	Blend if you want it smoother
	•	Jaggery can replace some sugar for deeper flavor
	•	Don’t overcook after adding garam masala
	•	Thickens more as it cools

Perfect for holiday turkey, spooned over warm brie, leftover holiday sliders, or a cheese / charcuterie board.
